title: What are the best sources for current affairs in UPSC preparation, except the Hindu paper?
reason: The user is asking for alternatives to The Hindu for current affairs, which directly aligns with the SatyaDheesh strategy of moving beyond passive newspaper reading to syllabus-mapped fact extraction.

matched_note.title: UPSC Daily Current Affairs & Editorial Analysis Strategy: The Hindu & Indian Express in 30 Minutes

drafted_comment:
The real issue is that reading the newspaper isn't enough; you need to filter the noise into exam-ready content. Instead of just reading more papers, focus on these three steps:

1. Syllabus Mapping: Only note down news that fits into GS1, GS2, GS3, or GS4 categories. If it doesn't fit a syllabus keyword, skip it.
2. Fact Extraction: For every major issue, ensure you have three pillars: a Constitutional article, a hard statistic, and a specific committee recommendation.
3. Active Recall: Don't just collect notes. Test yourself with daily MCQs to ensure you actually remember the facts.\n
(For free, syllabus-mapped daily notes and MCQs, check on satyadheesh portal)
